why: This script is the whole enforcement behind "a release has notes": the release job branches on its exit status, so a version with nothing written down cannot be tagged. Every edit below is a way it could start producing notes anyway — a heading anchor loosened until a subsection reads as a release, a refusal turned into a return, an empty section allowed through, or the entry point removed so the verdict never reaches an exit code.

mutations.name: the heading anchor is loosened
mutations.breaks: `## ` stops having to start a line, so a subsection inside a release — or the words '## ' anywhere in a bullet — becomes a release of its own, and one paragraph ships as the notes for the whole version.

mutations.name: any heading depth counts as a release
mutations.breaks: A `###` subsection heading is extracted as if it were a version, so the notes for a release become whichever subsection matched first.

mutations.name: a version with no section returns empty notes
mutations.breaks: The refusal that makes the release job fail becomes a successful run with nothing on stdout — a release published with blank notes, which is the exact outcome this script exists to prevent.
mutations.find:
raise ValueError(
        f"CHANGELOG.md has no section for {version} "
mutations.replace:
return ""
    raise ValueError(
        f"CHANGELOG.md has no section for {version} "

mutations.name: an empty section is accepted
mutations.breaks: A heading written before the notes were — the common half-finished state — passes as documented, and the release ships a version with an empty body.
mutations.find:
if not body.strip():
            raise ValueError(f"CHANGELOG.md section for {candidate} is empty")
mutations.replace:
if False:
            raise ValueError(f"CHANGELOG.md section for {candidate} is empty")

mutations.name: the missing-section status collapses into success
mutations.breaks: The exit status is the interface the release job branches on. Reporting 0 for a version with no section tells the job the notes were extracted.

mutations.name: an unreadable changelog is reported as a missing section
mutations.breaks: A broken repository is reported as an undocumented version, so a dry run that tolerates 'nothing written down yet' would tolerate a changelog it could not read at all.

mutations.name: the pre-release fallback stops falling back
mutations.breaks: A release candidate no longer finds the section for the release it is a candidate for, so rehearsing a release fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the notes.

mutations.name: the script's entry point is neutered
mutations.breaks: The verdict never reaches an exit code, and the release job reads success from a script that did nothing. A run that never happened prints no signature, which is how it is told apart from a run that passed.

mutations.name: the extraction returns the wrong body, checked under python3 -O
mutations.breaks: The checks used to be assert statements, which `python3 -O` strips: under that flag the self-test ran end to end and noticed nothing. This mutation is verified under -O on purpose, so the checks are proven to be real statements rather than assertions an interpreter flag can remove.
